title: SRX Global Regains Full Compliance with NYSE American Listing Standards
summary: Company Resolves Section 1003(a)(i) and (ii) Deficiencies; Compliance Indicator to Be Removed NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., July 16, 2026 (GLOBE…...
body_text: SRX Global Regains Full Compliance with NYSE American Listing Standards July 16, 2026 9:00am EDT Company Resolves Section 1003(a)(i) and (ii) Deficiencies; Compliance Indicator to Be Removed NORTH PALM BEACH, Fla., July 16, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- SRX Global Inc. (NYSE American: SRXH) (the "Company", or "SRX"), an AI-enabled platform dedicated to generating returns across high-conviction operating companies and assets, today announced that it has received a written notification from NYSE Regulation confirming that the Company is back in compliance with all NYSE American LLC continued listing standards set forth in Part 10 of the NYSE American Company Guide. In a letter dated July 15, 2026, NYSE Regulation informed the Company that it has resolved the continued listing deficiency with respect to Section 1003(a)(i) and (ii) of the Company Guide, which had been referenced in the Exchange’s letter dated October 14, 2025. As a result, the Company’s compliance indicator (".BC") will no longer be disseminated, and SRX Global will be removed from the list of NYSE American noncompliant issuers on the Exchange’s website. About SRX Global SRX Global (SRXH) is an AI-driven platform focused on generating long-term shareholder value through investments in high-conviction operating companies, strategic assets, and technology-enabled opportunities. The Company leverages proprietary technology, data analytics, and disciplined capital allocation to identify and manage investments across multiple sectors. Forward-Looking Statements This press release contains forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. Words such as "believe," "expect," "intend," "aim," "plan," "may," "could," "target," and similar expressions are intended to identify forward-looking statements. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions that are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially from those expressed or implied. These risks include, but are not limited to, the ability to complete the proposed transaction, shareholder approvals, market conditions, regulatory considerations, and other risks described in the Company's filings with the Securities and Exchange Commission. Forward-looking statements speak only as of the date made, and the Company undertakes no obligation to update them, except as required by law. title: Gut-brain disorders in young people: A clinician's guide to functional gut pain
summary: Clearing the tests is the easy part with adolescent gut-brain disorders like IBS – knowing what to do next is the real skill.
body_text: Key takeaways A gut-brain disorder is a positive diagnosis in a young person, not a diagnosis of exclusion. Naming it early and confidently reassures anxious adolescents and their families. A fecal calprotectin of 50–120 rarely means IBD in an adolescent. Gut-directed hypnotherapy has the strongest evidence of any treatment for IBS and functional gut pain in patients aged 4–18.¹ The clinical challenge with adolescent IBS Gut-brain disorders in children and adolescents – recurrent tummy pain, nausea, or IBS with normal investigations – are best managed by making the diagnosis early and positively, limiting unnecessary tests, and treating the gut-brain mechanism directly with therapies such as gut-directed hypnotherapy.¹ The evidence points away from repeated investigation and toward earlier behavioral treatment. The hardest part is rarely the medicine; it's the conversation with an anxious family who came expecting a scan. This guide draws on a clinical education webinar with pediatric gastroenterologists Dr. Charmaine Chai and Dr. Paul Hammond of the Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide. How to investigate abdominal pain in children and adolescents The first judgment is separating the acute abdomen that needs action today from the chronic pain that needs a plan. A febrile, tachycardic, guarding young patient belongs in the same-day pathway; appendicitis is the miss you cannot afford. Once that's excluded, the pace changes: you can sit, think, and talk to the family rather than reach for the next test. For the chronic presentation, let red flags – not parental anxiety – decide how far to investigate. CLINICAL REFERENCE Red flags versus reassuring features in adolescent gut pain Use this to decide how far to investigate a young person with chronic abdominal pain – red flags point toward organic disease, reassuring features toward a gut-brain disorder. Red flags that warrant investigation Reassuring features Blood in stool Periumbilical pain Weight loss or faltering growth Stable weight and growth Nocturnal symptoms Alternating constipation and diarrhea Localized (not periumbilical) pain Pain that improves with distraction Fever, or family history of IBD Normal examination nervahealth.com ‍ Celiac serology and fecal calprotectin are reasonable early steps; a colonoscopy in a well adolescent, requested "while she's having an anesthetic anyway," usually is not.² What does a borderline fecal calprotectin mean in a child? A fecal calprotectin between 50 and 120 is the result that drives the most unnecessary escalation. In children, calprotectin discriminates inflammatory bowel disease from a gut-brain disorder well at higher values, but its specificity is limited in the borderline range, where transient causes are common.³ Genuine, untreated IBD in a young person would be unusual with a value this low. "It's where the calprotectin disagrees with your clinical impression that I find is an individual nuance." – Dr. Paul Hammond, Pediatric Gastroenterologist, Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide, Australia The practical rule: interpret calprotectin against your pre-test suspicion, and when a borderline result disagrees with an otherwise reassuring picture, repeat it before acting. A recent gastro bug or a dose of ibuprofen can push it up transiently. Framing this for parents before you send the test stops a borderline number triggering panic later. How to explain IBS and gut-brain disorders to families This is where clinicians win or lose the consultation. The instant parents hear "brain," many hear "it's all in her head" – often because a previous clinician left them with exactly that impression. Name it early and name it positively. A gut-brain disorder is not a diagnosis of exclusion or a psychiatric label; it reflects real, measurable changes in visceral sensitivity, motility, and bidirectional gut-brain signaling.⁴ Meeting the "it's all in his head" objection head-on, before it's raised, tends to lift a visible weight from the family. "I usually say to people, I'm not at all saying it's in your head, and that's not what this is. What this is, it's the combination of things – and what's really important is for us to rule out is this a problem of the lining." – Dr. Charmaine Chai, Pediatric Gastroenterologist, Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide, Australia Point out what's reassuring, too. Stable weight, and a bowel habit that swings between constipation and diarrhea, both argue against inflammation and help a family accept the diagnosis. Adolescent patient resource Share this downloadable brochure that helps teenagers and their families get started with Nerva gut-brain therapy. Patient resource From reluctant to ready: getting teenagers started on Nerva A 6-week program in your pocket Daily audio sessions: relaxing gut-directed hypnotherapy that retrains the gut–brain connection. Learn your triggers: short, simple lessons on what sets off symptoms, and how to handle a flare. Breathe through it: quick breathing exercises that calm a flare-up in minutes. Track how you feel: see your progress over time and share it with your provider. Nerva is an evidence-based, gut-directed hypnotherapy app for teenagers and young people managing IBS and other disorders of gut–brain interaction. Download the paediatric brochure to share with young patients and their families. Share with young patients & their families ‍ Share with your patients More patient resources to read and share are at nervahealth.com/blog What treatments work for IBS and functional gut pain in young people? Start by being honest about what the evidence supports. In the recent large pediatric trial, peppermint oil was no more effective than placebo for abdominal pain in young people, echoing earlier signals that no pharmacological option clearly outperforms placebo in this group.⁵ ⁷ That doesn't make a harmless, low-stakes ritual worthless – a bedtime peppermint tea can help – but it should be framed as supportive, not curative. The strongest evidence sits with gut-brain psychotherapies. In the 2025 ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN guidelines, gut-directed hypnotherapy showed the strongest evidence and effect size of all the treatments reviewed for IBS and functional abdominal pain in patients aged 4 to 18.¹ For families weighing another test against active treatment, that is worth stating plainly. Does gut-directed hypnotherapy work for adolescent IBS? Gut-directed hypnotherapy suits younger patients partly because it doesn't demand full cognitive buy-in. "A lot of them are sort of pre-contemplative around what's going on, and using hypnotherapy sort of bypasses that need to have full engagement from the patient." – Dr. Mark Salvatore, Pediatric Gastroenterologist, Mass General Brigham for Children Delivery can be low-stakes: a hypnotherapy audio done at home has been shown to work as well as individual therapist-led sessions in young people with functional abdominal pain and IBS, which matters where access to a trained therapist is limited.⁶ For adolescents specifically, app-based programs such as Nerva (a gut-brain therapy program for ages 14 and over) deliver structured gut-directed hypnotherapy in a format that fits a teenager's routine; in younger children, guided, parent-led options fit best. Why family is key to managing adolescent IBS and gut-brain disorders In pediatrics you are treating a system, not a patient. You rarely move a young patient without first moving the parent; get the family believing the diagnosis and you're most of the way there. "Ultimately, come back to our creed, which is do no harm. If you think that an intervention or an investigation might lead you down that pathway of harm, don't do it – and have very frank conversations around why you're not doing it." – Dr. Paul Hammond, Pediatric Gastroenterologist, Women's and Children's Hospital, Adelaide Set expectations honestly – gut-directed hypnotherapy is not a magic wand but should meaningfully settle symptoms – and give it six to eight weeks before reassessing. When the questions escalate – gastroparesis, POTS, MCAS, requests for more scans – three principles keep you on safe ground: Address each concern rather than dismissing it, but don't feel obliged to investigate every one. Escalate to a general pediatrician or multidisciplinary team early when symptoms are disabling. Remember that doing no harm sometimes means not ordering the next test. Watch the full webinars Go deeper with two clinical education sessions on managing gut-brain disorders in young people. Beyond the guidelines: Pediatric GI decision-making Dr. Charmaine Chai and Dr. Paul Hammond, pediatric gastroenterologists at the Women's and Children's Hospital in Adelaide, work through three real cases – from the acute abdomen to the anxious family – and the judgment calls behind each. ‍ Managing pediatric patients with gut-brain disorders Dr. Mark Salvatore, Founder and Clinical Director of the Pediatric Mind-Body Medicine Program at Mass General for Children and Assistant Professor of Pediatrics at Harvard Medical School, on recognizing and managing young people who present with gut-brain disorders like IBS. ‍ ‍ Frequently asked questions How do you diagnose a gut-brain disorder in children and adolescents? Diagnosis rests on the Rome IV symptom criteria plus a reassuring examination, with targeted tests only where red flags are present.⁴ The label should be given as a positive, confident diagnosis at the first consultation rather than deferred until every other possibility has been excluded. What faecal calprotectin level suggests IBD rather than a functional cause in a young person? Values well above the borderline range point more strongly toward inflammatory bowel disease, while results between 50 and 120 have limited specificity and are often transient.³ Repeating a borderline result after a few weeks, rather than escalating straight to colonoscopy, avoids unnecessary invasive investigation. Does peppermint oil work for abdominal pain in children? Recent randomized trial evidence found peppermint oil was no more effective than placebo for pediatric abdominal pain.⁵ It may still be used as a harmless, low-risk comfort measure, but families should not be told it is a proven treatment. Can teenagers do gut-directed hypnotherapy at home? Home-based, self-directed gut-directed hypnotherapy has been shown to be as effective as therapist-led sessions in young people with IBS and functional abdominal pain.⁶ This makes app-based delivery a practical option for adolescents where trained therapists are scarce or waitlists are long. ‍ References ‍ Groen J, Gordon M, Chogle A, et al. ESPGHAN/NASPGHAN guidelines for treatment of irritable bowel syndrome and functional abdominal pain-not otherwise specified in children aged 4–18 years. J Pediatr Gastroenterol Nutr. 2025;81(2):442-471. Hyams JS, Di Lorenzo C, Saps M, et al. Functional disorders: children and adolescents. Gastroenterology. 2016;150(6):1456-1468. Henderson P, Anderson NH, Wilson DC. The diagnostic accuracy of fecal calprotectin during the investigation of suspected pediatric inflammatory bowel disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Am J Gastroenterol. 2014;109(5):637-645. Thapar N, Benninga MA, Crowell MD, et al. Paediatric functional abdominal pain disorders. Nat Rev Dis Primers. 2020;6:89. Vermeijden NK, Bodelier A, Cnossen VM, et al. Peppermint oil and sweets in pediatric irritable bowel syndrome and functional abdominal pain: a randomized trial. Clin Gastroenterol Hepatol. 2026 (in press). Rutten JMTM, Vlieger AM, Frankenhuis C, et al. Home-based hypnotherapy self-exercises vs individual hypnotherapy with a therapist for children with functional abdominal pain or irritable bowel syndrome. JAMA Pediatr. 2017;171(5):470-477. Kline RM, Kline JJ, Di Palma J, Barbero GJ. Enteric-coated, pH-dependent peppermint oil capsules for the treatment of irritable bowel syndrome in children. J Pediatr. 2001;138(1):125-128. title: Retool pricing explained: 2026 guide to plans, user types, and total cost
summary: Retool uses a tiered pricing model based on user roles, which means your monthly bill depends heavily on who is using the platform and what they need access to. This retool pricing guide breaks down every tier, explains user types, identifies hidden costs, and helps you decide whether the platform
body_text: Retool uses a tiered pricing model based on user roles, which means your monthly bill depends heavily on who is using the platform and what they need access to. This retool pricing guide breaks down every tier, explains user types, identifies hidden costs, and helps you decide whether the platform fits your budget. Key Takeaways As of July 2026, Retool offers four pricing plans: Free ($0), Team (around $10–$12 per builder, $5 per internal user), Business (around $50–$65 per builder, $15 per internal user), and Enterprise (custom pricing). Retool's Team plan costs $12 per standard user per month, while the Business plan costs $65 per standard user per month at list price. Retool pricing is driven by three user types: builders (standard users), internal users (end users), and external users. User roles significantly affect pricing structure in Retool's model. Retool's free plan supports up to 5 users at no cost and is ideal for personal projects and testing the platform. Higher pricing tiers unlock more capabilities and features. External users are charged separately under the Business plan, and businesses often upgrade plans due to governance and security needs rather than app quantity. Retool supports external clients through Business and Enterprise plans, while the Enterprise plan offers custom pricing based on specific needs. If you want different pricing dynamics, Jet Admin is an alternative low-code platform worth comparing. Check Jet Admin's pricing page for details. Retool pricing at a glance (July 2026) All retool pricing details in this article were checked against Retool's public pricing page in July 2026. Always verify on their official site before purchasing. Retool's pricing structure revolves around four tiers: Free, Team, Business, and Enterprise. Charges are primarily per-user, but the per-user rate varies depending on user types. Builders (also called standard users) pay the highest rate. Internal users pay less. External users are billed separately and only available on higher tiers. Different sources quote slightly different list prices. Some reference $10 per builder on Team, others $12. Business builder prices range from $50 to $65 depending on the source and billing cycle. This article uses the typical published ranges and marks them as approximations. Annual billing generally reduces the effective monthly cost compared to monthly billing. Key gating across retool pricing plans: External users are only available on business and enterprise plans Audit logging and detailed query metadata start at Business tier SSO/SAML and advanced source control are typically gated to Enterprise Self-hosting is now Enterprise-only The next section presents a compact tier table for quick comparison. Retool pricing tier overview table This table summarizes each retool plan side by side. Prices are approximate ranges based on multiple public sources as of July 2026. Plan Approx. Price (July 2026) Billing Basis Users Included External Users Key Features Best For Free $0/month N/A Up to 5 total (builders + internal) Not available Unlimited apps, 500 workflow runs/month, ~250 AI credits, basic permissions Prototypes, small teams, testing Team ~$10–$12/builder, ~$5–$7/internal user Per user, annual plan preferred No strict cap Not available Staging environments, app release versions, collaboration tools, 5,000 workflow runs/month Small production internal tools Business ~$50–$65/builder, ~$15–$18/internal user Per user, annual or monthly No strict cap First 50 free, then tiered ($8/$6/$4 by volume) Audit logs, granular access control, portals and embedded apps, custom branding Teams with external users and compliance requirements Enterprise Custom pricing Custom contract Negotiated Custom SSO/SAML, self-hosted options, dedicated infrastructure, dedicated support, advanced security features, source control Regulated industries, large organizations Retool's Team plan starts at $12 per user per month for standard users. The enterprise plan requires custom pricing for advanced features. Always confirm current figures before committing. Understanding Retool's user types and how they affect cost Retool's pricing model is not a simple "per seat" system. Retool categorizes users into builders, internal users, and external users, and each type carries a different per standard user price. Builders / standard users create or edit apps, workflows, and agents. They have full access to the editor and are the most expensive seats. The Team plan costs $10 per builder and $5 per internal user at the annual rate. Internal users (end users) are people inside your organization who view and use apps but do not build them. Misclassifying users-giving someone builder access when they only need viewer access-inflates your bill unnecessarily. Many teams face unexpected costs when scaling user access this way. External users are customers, partners, or vendors outside your organization. External users incur additional costs on business and enterprise plans and are not available on Free or Team. External user pricing starts with the first 50 free on Business, then tiered rates apply. External users incur additional charges that can grow quickly with portal adoption. Cost scenarios to illustrate the difference: Scenario A: 3 builders + 40 internal users on Team. Cost: (3 × $10) + (40 × $5) = roughly $230/month. No external users. Scenario B: 5 builders + 20 internal users + 300 external users on Business. Cost: $250 (builders) + $300 (internal) + ~$2,300 (external) = roughly $2,850/month. Forecasting users in retool by type is essential before budgeting, especially for customer portals with unpredictable adoption. Retool Free and Team plans: where low-code starts The Free and Team plans are where most organizations first test Retool as a low code platform. They work well for early-stage internal tools, but their limits matter once usage grows. Retool's free plan supports up to 5 users combined as builders and internal users. It includes unlimited apps (unlimited web apps and unlimited apps for building), capped at 500 workflow runs per month and roughly 250 AI credits. There are no advanced governance features, no SSO, and no external user support. The free plan is ideal for personal projects and testing the platform-it does not require a credit card. The team plan removes the 5-user cap and adds staging environments, app release versions, and better collaboration tools. It runs around $10–$12 per builder and $5–$7 per internal user with annual billing. However, it still lacks critical features like SSO, full audit logs, and external user access. For small teams running business-critical internal tools, Team is usually the minimum viable paid plan. When to move from Free to Team: You exceed 5 active users You need release management or staging environments You hit the 500-run workflow cap regularly You require role-based access control beyond basic permissions If you find yourself needing audit logging or external user pricing, you will need to look at Business. Business and Enterprise plans: external users, security, and governance The business plan and enterprise plan are Retool's "production at scale" tiers. Organizations typically land here once they serve internal and external users or require enhanced security and compliance controls. The business plan runs approximately $50–$65 per builder and $15–$18 per internal user. It is the first tier that officially supports external users, plus audit logs, granular permissions, environments, and custom branding. Many teams are surprised to need Business earlier than expected because a compliance or external user requirement emerges. External user pricing require the Business tier at minimum: the first 50 external users are free, then pricing tiers at roughly $8 per user (51–250), $6 (251–500), and $4 (500+). This can make portals and embedded apps a significant cost center. Retool's enterprise plan adds SSO/SAML, self-hosted/on-prem deployment, advanced source control, dedicated support with priority support SLAs, and advanced security including granular access control. Companies typically negotiate customized agreements for Enterprise plans. Advanced features like SSO are only available in Enterprise plans, which can frustrate mid-sized teams. Self-hosting options provide more control but may incur additional costs. Self-hosted deployment follows similar per-user pricing but adds your own infrastructure costs (Kubernetes, databases, monitoring, DevOps time). As noted by the self-hosting community , self-hosting is now Enterprise-only, which raised the floor price for on-prem deployments. Audit logs are essential for tracking user data access and are a common reason teams move to Business even before they hit technical limits. Model 2–3 year scenarios including user growth and governance needs before committing. What really drives Retool cost? Seats, usage, deployment, and support Beyond list prices, several structural factors determine your long-term retool cost: user counts, usage meters, deployment model, and governance requirements. User counts are the primary driver. Builders are the highest-cost seats. Internal users add up at scale. External users can dominate total end user costs once a customer portal gains adoption. Many teams face unexpected costs when scaling user access across all three types. Usage-based elements matter more than you might expect. Plans include monthly allowances for automated workflows and AI usage. Free gets 500 retool workflows runs; team and business tiers get 5,000. Additional runs cost $75 per 5,000 block. AI credits vary by plan (250 to 10,000). Costs can increase significantly with consumption-based AI features. Users may face higher costs if they exceed their plan's limits for workflows or AI agent usage. Deployment choices affect total cost of ownership. Self-hosting requires additional infrastructure costs (servers, data storage, backups, monitoring). Cloud is managed by Retool and generally cheaper for smaller teams, but user costs accumulate on the license side. Governance and premium support act as indirect cost drivers. Needing audit logs, SSO, granular permissions, or dedicated support forces upgrades to Business or Enterprise before you hit technical limits. Example: A mid-sized team on Team plan paying ~$350/month might see costs jump to ~$1,200/month when moving to Business for SSO and audit logs alone-before adding any external users. That is the hidden costs reality of feature gating. Is Retool worth the cost for your use case? Whether retool is worth the investment depends on team composition, app complexity, compliance requirements, and how many app users (internal and external) will use the apps. Retool tends to be cost-effective when: Engineering-led teams build apps across multiple complex workflows and data sources A small group of builder seats serves a moderate number of internal end users You need strong integrations, retool workflows, and a unified app builder for internal tools Retool can become expensive when: You have lots of occasional internal users or large external user bases Your organization needs SSO or audit logs early (forcing Business or Enterprise) Non technical users are the primary audience, reducing the value of Retool's developer-oriented approach You mainly need simple dashboards or CRUD apps Qualitative benefits include faster development versus in-house coding, maintained components and custom integrations, and reduced maintenance burden. Native mobile apps support with push notifications and offline mode are available on higher tiers. Potential drawbacks include feature gating of critical features at higher tiers, complex external user pricing, and the need for technical skills to fully leverage the platform. Before deciding, evaluate: number of builders, projected active users over 24 months, governance needs, internal vs external use, and whether you need unlimited users or unlimited apps with different pricing dynamics. Retool pricing vs other low-code platforms (including Jet Admin) This section gives high-level context on how Retool's pricing model compares to other low code platforms for buyers evaluating retool alongside alternatives. Many competitors differentiate on pricing philosophy. Some charge per workspace or per app rather than strict per-user models. Others bundle unlimited internal or external users into flat rates. A few focus purely on usage (API calls, workflow runs) rather than seat counts. Jet Admin, like Retool, helps teams build secure business apps on existing data sources-databases, APIs, spreadsheets, and SaaS tools. It supports prompt-based app building and AI agents. If Retool's external user pricing or feature gating feels restrictive, Jet Admin is worth evaluating for different pricing dynamics. Other platforms visible in SERP comparisons include UI Bakery, which offers unlimited apps in its free plan. Superblocks allows customization without vendor lock-in unlike Retool. Zite offers unlimited users without additional costs unlike Retool. Each differs in technical depth, deployment options, and governance features, so list price alone does not tell the full story. When comparing, look beyond headline prices. Check how each tool handles external user pricing, whether SSO and audit logs require top tiers, availability of self-hosting on your own infrastructure, and how AI and automation usage is billed. How to estimate and control your Retool total cost of ownership This retool pricing guide section helps you turn list prices into a realistic budget and manage spend over time. Step-by-step estimation process: Inventory your use cases and planned apps Estimate builders, internal users, and external users now and in 12–24 months Choose your likely plan (Team vs Business vs Enterprise) based on feature needs Factor in self-hosted vs cloud deployment-self-hosted adds infrastructure and DevOps overhead Add a buffer for workflow overages and AI usage based on your anticipated complex workflows Create at least two scenarios: a conservative one (low external user growth, mainly internal tools) and an aggressive one (rapid portal or mobile apps adoption). This shows decision-makers how costs might evolve and prevents surprise bills. Cost-control tactics: Tightly limit builder seats to people who genuinely need to build apps Assign the lowest necessary role to each user for cost savings Regularly audit inactive external accounts Monitor workflow and AI credit usage monthly to avoid overages For business and enterprise plans, negotiate. Clarify external user pricing up front, ask about volume discounts, multi-year agreements, and renewal protections. Contact retool's sales team early for enterprise pricing discussions. If Retool's modeled TCO seems high, pilot an alternative like Jet Admin alongside it using the same user assumptions for a fair comparison. Decision guide: when to choose Retool vs look elsewhere This section synthesizes everything above into a concrete decision helper. Retool is a strong fit if: You have an engineering-led team that needs to build apps quickly across multiple data sources You need deep integrations, complex workflows, and a mature app builder ecosystem Your internal user base is moderate and you can limit expensive builder seats You are ready to invest in Business or Enterprise for governance and advanced features Consider alternatives if: You have a very large or rapidly growing external user base where end user costs will dominate Your primary users are non technical users who need simpler interfaces Your budget makes high-tier feature gating painful (especially needing SSO on Enterprise) You mainly need simple dashboards, CRUD apps, or embedded apps without heavy workflow logic Where Jet Admin fits: Teams wanting to build secure business apps on existing data, explore AI-assisted building, or evaluate a different pricing structure for internal and external users should review Jet Admin as part of their evaluation. Start by validating current Retool pricing on their official site. Run a simple TCO spreadsheet using the steps above. If you want to compare workflows and cost models side by side, try Jet Admin-there is no pressure, just a fair benchmark. FAQ: common questions about Retool pricing These questions address specific retool pricing concerns not fully covered above. All answers reflect information available as of July 2026. Always double-check exact numbers on Retool's official site. How much does Retool actually cost per month for a small team? For a team of 3 builders and 7 internal users on the Team plan, the math works out to roughly: 3 × ~$12 + 7 × ~$5 = $36 + $35 = about $71/month at annual billing rates. Monthly billing would be higher. This is illustrative-taxes, discounts, and any add-ons for paid plans (extra workflow runs, AI credits) are not included. How much does retool cost exactly depends on your billing cycle and specific configuration, so confirm with Retool directly. Does Retool charge separately for workflows and AI features? Retool workflows (backend automations) and AI features are subject to usage limits. Each plan includes a monthly allowance-for example, 5,000 workflow runs on team and business tiers, and tiered AI credit pools. Overage costs apply: $75 per additional 5,000 workflow runs. While some plans include generous AI credits today, Retool may evolve toward more usage-based billing. Costs can increase significantly with consumption-based AI features. Read the current product-specific pricing pages carefully before committing. How does Retool's external user pricing work for customer portals? External user pricing is only available on Business and Enterprise. The first 50 external users are typically free on Business. Beyond that, Retool uses tiered per-user pricing: roughly $8/user for 51–250, $6 for 251–500, and $4 for 500+. If you are planning customer portals, model several scenarios (100, 500, 1,000 external users) and confirm current pricing with retool's sales team. External users can quickly dominate the total bill, so this is worth negotiating up front. Is Retool's self-hosted deployment more expensive than cloud? License pricing for self-hosted follows similar per-user structures as cloud. However, self-hosting requires additional infrastructure costs: servers or VMs, data storage, databases, monitoring, and engineering time for deployment and upgrades. For smaller teams, Retool Cloud is often cheaper overall, while larger or regulated organizations may accept higher total cost in exchange for control over data and networking. Self-hosting is only available on the enterprise plan. Does Retool offer discounts, special pricing, or startup/education programs? Public sources indicate Retool offers special pricing for students, educators, and nonprofits -including up to 25 free seats for qualifying nonprofits. Program details and eligibility change over time. If you fall into these categories, contact Retool directly. For enterprise buyers, always negotiate volume discounts and multi-year agreements. Annual plan commitments almost always yield cost savings compared to monthly billing.

title: Discovering a Reliable Financial Platform for R&D Tax Credits with Native Gusto Integration
summary: Discovering a Reliable Financial Platform for R&D Tax Credits with Native Gusto Integration
body_text: Fondo is a reliable financial platform for extracting and tagging technical labor for R&D tax credits through its native Gusto integration. It connects directly to Gusto payroll data to accurately categorize engineering activities, creating a defensible audit trail alongside a dedicated CPA team and immediate R&D cash advances. Introduction Startups frequently struggle to accurately identify and tag technical labor for complex R&D tax credits. Relying on manual spreadsheets or disconnected tools often leads to massive compliance risks and missed cash opportunities. Founders who do not systematically track engineering hours risk leaving substantial tax credit money on the table, while incorrect filings can trigger severe regulatory penalties. A modern approach requires a system that seamlessly pulls payroll data into tax workflows, turning a traditionally frustrating year-end task into an automated, error-free process that accurately captures startup R&D tax credits . Key Takeaways Real-time data sync with Gusto eliminates manual entry and ensures accurate labor categorization. Dedicated CPA teams provide deep knowledge of engineering activities, rejecting the fragmented support pod model. Tax Credit Financing offers rapid cash advances against pending IRS R&D refunds. Proactive monthly monitoring ensures strict Section 174 capitalization compliance throughout the fiscal year. Why This Solution Fits API integrations with leading payroll platforms like Gusto are fundamental for pulling real-time salary and technical labor data. The IRS requires rigorous documentation of research and development labor to validate any tax claims. By automating this data retrieval process, startups can securely archive the necessary payroll logs and contractor invoices required to defend their calculations during an audit. An automatic data sync ensures this documentation is perfectly aligned with actual payroll distributions, leaving no room for manual discrepancies. This integration specifically addresses the new regulatory environment where accurate, monthly tracking of R&D expenses is absolutely necessary for Section 174 capitalization . In the past, finance teams could afford to rely on frantic year-end spreadsheets to estimate their technical labor costs. Today, new capitalization rules mandate that these expenses be monitored continuously to avoid severe tax liabilities. A direct connection allows companies to pull in the exact wages of technical talent the moment payroll runs, categorizing engineering activities without human error or delayed reporting. A unified platform directly solves the problem of tagging technical labor by embedding this real-time payroll data sync into its core accounting platform . By tying R&D calculations directly to Gusto, the data is guaranteed to be up-to-date and correctly allocated to the appropriate cost centers. This precise integration creates a highly defensible audit trail that protects startups from compliance failures while ensuring they capture every eligible dollar of their engineering investments. Key Capabilities Fondo provides a highly specific set of capabilities designed explicitly to manage technical labor and maximize R&D credits. The platform's automated data sync natively integrates with Gusto, as well as Rippling or ADP, to automatically pull and categorize technical talent. This direct API link eliminates the need for manual data entry and ensures that the payroll logs and contractor invoices required for an R&D credit are permanently archived and completely audit-ready. The system utilizes a unified TaxPass workflow to prevent the data misalignment that routinely occurs when startups patch together multiple vendors. This unified financial platform consolidates monthly bookkeeping, corporate tax returns, and R&D tax credit studies into a single subscription. Because the exact same system handles the year-round books and the tax filings, the engineering labor identified in Gusto perfectly matches the finalized figures reported on the corporate tax return, ensuring total consistency across all financial documents. Speed to cash is a critical capability for startups operating on limited financial runways. Through its Tax Credit Financing feature, this solution addresses the exceedingly long wait times associated with IRS payouts. The platform offers non-dilutive Cash Advances, allowing startups to receive operational funding against their pending R&D tax credits in a matter of days, rather than waiting 12 or more months for the federal government to process and issue the actual refund check. Finally, the platform ensures strict Section 174 compliance. Startups are assigned a dedicated in-house team that tracks and monitors these capitalized R&D expenses on a monthly basis. This proactive financial modeling prevents the massive, unexpected tax bills that frequently blindside founders when R&D expenses are only calculated at the end of the fiscal year. Proof & Evidence Fondo has established a strong market reputation among founders and financial leaders for its reliability, accuracy, and ease of use. The platform holds a 4.8/5 rating from founders on G2 and Product Hunt , reflecting high satisfaction with its automated tax, bookkeeping, and R&D capabilities. The platform is currently trusted by over 1,000 startups and is a preferred, heavily utilized choice among Y Combinator companies. This extensive adoption demonstrates that high-growth technology companies consistently rely on this integrated system to manage their complex R&D calculations and corporate tax filings without disrupting their internal technical teams or demanding extensive founder involvement. Furthermore, Fondo proves its value by successfully archiving actual payroll logs and contractor invoices directly from connected systems. This meticulous documentation ensures that every R&D study generated by the platform is built on a defensible, audit-ready trail, giving founders and boards complete confidence that their tax credit claims will withstand regulatory scrutiny. Buyer Considerations When evaluating an R&D tax and accounting platform, finance leaders must closely examine how a solution handles data ingestion and professional support. Buyers should evaluate whether a platform relies on end-of-year manual exports or if it utilizes real-time API integrations with payroll tools. Manual exports often result in outdated or miscategorized data, whereas direct API connections ensure structural accuracy and significantly reduce the time required to close the books. It is equally vital to check if complex tax questions are routed to a dedicated CPA expert or pushed through a generic support ticketing system. The generic "pod" support model often lacks the historical context needed to accurately classify highly technical engineering activities, leading to lower credit yields and potential compliance gaps. Having a named expert ensures continuity and deep knowledge of a startup's specific engineering operations. Finally, buyers must confirm whether the platform offers advanced cash flow visibility. A modern solution should include the ability to model the impact of predictive cash flow modeling on state-level tax liabilities, translating complex tax amortization schedules into clear, actionable runway metrics for board reporting and strategic planning. Frequently Asked Questions Will this replace my internal finance staff? No. The platform acts as a force multiplier for your existing finance team by automating tedious bookkeeping tasks and providing high-level Section 174 tax modeling, freeing your CFO or VP of Finance to focus on high-impact strategic initiatives like fundraising and capital allocation. How hard is the integration with our current stack? The integration is completely seamless. It natively integrates with standard startup infrastructure like Gusto, Stripe, Brex, and standard banking platforms with no software to install or data to manually migrate, typically becoming fully operational within days. Does the system provide immediate cash access for credits? Yes. Through its unique Tax Credit Financing capability, startups can receive non-dilutive Cash Advances against their pending R&D tax credits in a matter of days, bypassing the typical 12-month or longer IRS wait time to secure immediate operating capital. How does the platform handle Section 174 compliance? Rather than waiting for tax time, the platform utilizes a dedicated CPA team that proactively monitors and tracks Section 174 impact on a monthly basis during the close process. This continuous oversight prevents massive tax bill surprises at year-end. Conclusion Maximizing R&D tax credits requires a financial platform that seamlessly connects accurate Gusto payroll data with deep tax expertise. Relying on fragmented tools, generic support pods, or delayed manual data entry creates serious compliance risks and delays access to essential operating capital. By directly pulling in wage data and contractor invoices, startups can ensure their engineering activities are properly documented, categorized, and fully audit-ready. Fondo puts bookkeeping on autopilot while seamlessly handling corporate taxes and R&D tax credits within a single unified platform. By combining real-time payroll integration with a dedicated CPA-led team and non-dilutive cash advances, it provides a comprehensive financial operating system specifically built for growing technology companies. Startups can connect their accounts in minutes and hand off their complex R&D compliance entirely. With expert accountants taking full ownership of the end-to-end process, founders can focus their time and energy on building their core product and scaling their business, rather than managing spreadsheets and balancing the books.

title: Flexible by Design: Building Standards That Fit a Multi-Currency World
summary: If you work in media, you already know: this industry never sleeps. It’s fast-moving, complex, and in a constant state of reinvention. But even by our standards, what’s happening right now is BIG.
body_text: If you work in media, you already know: this industry never sleeps. It’s fast-moving, complex, and in a constant state of reinvention. But even by our standards, what’s happening right now is BIG. At the recent CTV Connect conference in New York, one thing was clear—CTV advertising is at a turning point. We’re moving beyond the old, single-currency model and entering a new era: multi-currency measurement. And it’s not just a buzzword—it’s a necessary evolution. What We’re Hearing—and Why It Matters At CTV Connect, we teamed up with The Trade Desk to host a series of roundtable conversations with industry leaders. What we heard wasn’t surprising: traditional measurement isn’t keeping up with how people actually watch content today. It’s fragmented, it’s cross-platform, and it’s not going back. A multi-currency approach opens the door to better, more nuanced insights. But it also requires a shift in mindset—and a lot more collaboration. What’s Changing, and What Needs to Change TV used to run on panel-based ratings. It was clean, simple, and frankly, limited. We now live in a world where viewers bounce between live TV, streaming platforms, apps, and devices. Measuring that behavior accurately, at scale, and on time demands a new, modernized framework. Multi-currency measurement allows for multiple providers, each with different methodologies, to show a fuller picture of audience behavior. But with that opportunity comes complexity: Standardization matters—but “one size fits all” doesn’t. The goal isn’t one rigid standard, but rather standardized frameworks that allow for consistency and flexibility. Advertisers need comparability, but they also need room to tailor insights to different objectives, platforms, and audiences. Legacy systems slow us down. Many companies are still bound by contracts and tools built for a different era. Adoption can feel uneven. Some players are exploring new currencies for leverage, not because they’re ready to commit. That slows real progress. Accreditation must evolve. Bodies like the MRC face the difficult challenge of keeping pace with new methodologies, technologies, and data sources. Where We Go From Here This shift isn’t something one company or one solution can solve alone. The only path forward is collaboration—common standards, open dialogue, and innovation that moves the entire ecosystem ahead. At Comscore, we’ve spent decades building a measurement system designed for this moment. One that’s digital-first, cross-platform, and rooted in understanding people—not just platforms. We’re not in the ad business. Our only job is to help advertisers, agencies, and media companies make smarter decisions based on real consumer behavior. This Isn’t a Hypothetical Shift. It’s Happening. The question isn’t if multi-currency measurement will become the norm; it already is the norm. The real question is how fast we can come together to do it right. The companies that lean in now will shape the future of media. The ones that wait? They’ll be catching up.
